title: Surface, BufferQueue, Gralloc, and Synchronisation Fences Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies surface, bufferqueue, gralloc, and synchronisation fences?
options: Respect producer-consumer ownership, Surface lifecycle, bounded queues, allocation usage, and fences before tuning buffer count.
questions.answer: Respect producer-consumer ownership, Surface lifecycle, bounded queues, allocation usage, and fences before tuning buffer count.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: BufferQueue normally copies each completed pixel buffer into the consumer process.
questions.explanation: Treating Surface lifecycle as identical to Activity lifecycle can render into a destroyed queue during pause, rotation, or window replacement.

questions.prompt: What does a release fence protect?
questions.answer: It indicates when the consumer has finished using a buffer so the producer can safely reuse it.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
